body: I approve the 7 cuts and I approve the dualcaster mage and displace adds and respective recommended cuts. my main issue is that a low bracket 4 deck should win between turns 5 and 6, or at least have the winning pieces on the board/hand by turn 7. however, our simulation shows that winning by turn 8 only happens 11.8% of the time. can't we do anything else to speed up the win?

**Review done, and the iteration loop is done: 8 deck variants, 2 sim passes, 20,000 games each. The updated 99 is consistent, legal, and sound. The full power package is the right build — it triples the tempo of combo closes vs the tuned-down list. To finish, I need you to accept the 7 named cuts that make room for the 7 accepted power adds. Two optional redundancy swaps are on the table too. Total purchase list lands at ~$460.**

## 1. The named cuts (accept or block each line)

You accepted the adds; each cut below needs your line-item acceptance before I write anything.

- [ ] Mystical Tutor in / **Brainstorm out** — the tutors replace raw selection with on-demand combo assembly
- [ ] Solve the Equation in / **Ponder out** — same reason
- [ ] Merchant Scroll in / **Whirlwind of Thought out** — 5-mana draw engine was the clunkiest draw slot
- [ ] Panoptic Mirror in / **Insurrection out** — frees the big-mana slot and saves the $14.48 buy
- [ ] Mox Amber in / **Fellwar Stone out** — Amber is a 0-mana rock; 21 legendary Wizards plus Gandalf keep it live
- [ ] Fierce Guardianship in / **Arcane Denial out** — free counter replaces the weakest paid counter
- [ ] Ancient Tomb in / **1 Plains out (5 → 4)** — pip census says white is the light color: 13 W pips vs 55 U and 23 R. After the cut we keep 15 white sources out of 36 lands for those 13 pips.

Optional (from the redundancy iteration, section 4):

- [ ] Dualcaster Mage in / Preordain out — second combo starter; we own a copy (committed to aziza, duplicate is ~$1)
- [ ] Displace in / Frantic Search out — second blink spell, ~$0.50; only worth it together with Dualcaster

## 2. Consistency / correctness / soundness review

- **Count and legality**: exactly 99 cards, no unintended duplicates, every card commander-legal and inside WUR identity (checked against the 2026-08-15 mirror).
- **One real correctness catch**: Naru Meha's copy trigger is an **enters-the-battlefield trigger**, not a cast trigger. The combo lines in this thread were described correctly (flash Naru in response to your own spell), but my first sim draft awarded wins with Naru already on the battlefield — a state where the loop cannot start, because her trigger fires after the original spell has left the stack. I fixed the model: all Naru/Dualcaster lines now require the creature **in hand**. Commander Spellbook's data confirms this — its combo entries list Naru's required zone as hand.
- **Practical consequence for play**: never pre-cast Naru Meha as a body. Hold her to flash in response to your own Ghostly Flicker or Sublime Epiphany.
- **Spellbook re-check on the final 99 — 7 confirmed combos**:
  1. Naru Meha + Ghostly Flicker (7 mana, Naru in hand) — infinite magecraft
  2. Naru Meha + Sublime Epiphany (Naru in hand) — infinite magecraft and draw
  3. Fury Storm + Storm-Kiln Artist — infinite Treasure (needs 1 prior commander cast)
  4. Fury Storm + Archmage Emeritus — draws the deck
  5. Fury Storm + Deekah — infinite Fractal tokens
  6. Panoptic Mirror + Temporal Mastery — infinite turns lock
  7. Panoptic Mirror + Alrund's Epiphany — infinite turns lock
- **Game Changers**: the final list has **4** (Mystical Tutor, Fierce Guardianship, Ancient Tomb, Panoptic Mirror). Bracket 4 has no GC cap. The label stays **4-**, and per our relabel rule a 4-GC deck cannot be labeled below 4-. This is now a true low-B4 deck, which is what you asked for when you took the power package.

## 3. Power iteration — does the package actually speed up closes?

Goldfish Monte Carlo, 20,000 games per variant. A "close" means a confirmed infinite combo is online with mana to run it and a payoff to convert it. The numbers below are the realistic pass (draw engines and a simple mulligan on). Read them comparatively: the model ignores Gandalf's free casts, Vivi burn, and extra-turn beats, so real close rates are higher across the board.

| Variant | close by T7 | by T8 | by T9 | never (T14) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| V0 — accepted swaps, no power package | 1.8% | 3.7% | 6.7% | 74.2% |
| V2 — tutors only | 3.5% | 7.5% | 12.7% | 58.7% |
| V3 — fast mana only | 2.5% | 5.2% | 8.2% | 73.2% |
| **V1 — full package (the list above)** | **5.5%** | **11.0%** | **17.8%** | **48.5%** |
| V6 — V1 + Dualcaster Mage | 5.6% | 11.6% | 18.6% | 47.0% |
| V7 — V1 + Dualcaster + Displace | 5.8% | 11.8% | 19.1% | 46.4% |

What the table says: the tutors are the biggest single lever (V2 vs V0), fast mana alone does little (V3), and the full package roughly **triples** every close-rate column vs the tuned-down deck. I also tested keeping Time Stretch over Ghostly Flicker — a statistical tie, so the accepted Flicker swap stands.

## 4. The redundancy iteration

The near-miss scan of the final 99 shows the biggest open class is Flicker-partner creatures (Dualcaster Mage, Archaeomancer, Izzet Chronarch, Mnemonic Wall...). I tested the two cleanest: **Displace alone adds nothing** (the tutor suite already finds the blink spell on demand), while **Dualcaster Mage adds a real but small lift** (+0.6 points at T8) because combo starters are creatures our tutors cannot fetch. Both together are the best list I found (V7), but the gain over V1 is under 1 point per turn column. My recommendation: take Dualcaster, skip Displace unless you want the last decimal. Both are optional lines in the checklist; V1 as listed is already the build you approved.

## 5. Money

Power package buys: Mystical Tutor $16.23, Solve the Equation $3.77, Merchant Scroll $4.95, Panoptic Mirror $26.39, Mox Amber $79.81, Fierce Guardianship $55.11, Ancient Tomb $134.91 = **+$321.17**. The Insurrection cut removes a $14.48 buy, and the earlier Flicker swap removed $2.63. New purchase-list total: **~$460** (prices as quoted earlier today).

**All five answers are below. I recommend five swaps. Three of the adds are cards you already own. The purchase list moves up about $11, to roughly $156. A new confirmation replaces the earlier one — please answer the new one.**

**1. Turbulent Steppe / Turbulent Springs — you are right, and I found the process gap.**

Both are owned (Secrets of Strixhaven Commander, added to the collection in April 2026). They are typed duals that enter untapped when your opponents control eight or more lands. In four-player games that is true from about turn 3, so they behave as untapped duals almost all game.

Why the draft missed them: I build draft manabases by hand from the familiar land cycles, and no script covers the draft stage. The candidate pool never surfaces lands, and `manabase_check.py` needs a written `deck.json`, which only exists after approval. Four built decks do use the cycle, but our single copies of Steppe and Springs are each already committed to two decks, so the "free owned lands" pass skipped them. That is why we keep missing them.

The fix: I added a mandatory draft-stage step to the new-deck pipeline — sweep the owned collection plus the mirror for every owned nonbasic land inside the deck's color identity before posting any manabase. Stored as memory, so it applies to every future deck.

Proposed swaps (both are duplicate buys, like Battlefield Forge was):
- **Turbulent Steppe in, Battlefield Forge out** (+$3.82 net). No self-damage, and its Mountain and Plains subtypes turn on Clifftop Retreat and Glacial Fortress.
- **Turbulent Springs in, Shivan Reef out** (+$5.05). Island and Mountain subtypes turn on Sulfur Falls; Shivan Reef returns to the free pool.

**2. Erode — yes, add it.** It is a {W} instant: destroy target creature or planeswalker; its controller may fetch a tapped basic. The drawback is tiny in commander. You own two copies and one is free (the other is in slivers). Swap: **Erode in, Aminatou's Augury out** — Augury was the weakest payoff slot (eight mana, wins nothing on resolution). $0.

**3. One more board wipe — yes: Raise the Palisade.** You own two copies and one is free (the other is in tidal-legion). Choose Wizard and it bounces every other creature while our board survives — except Storm-Kiln Artist, who is a Dwarf **Shaman**, not a Wizard; he comes back for 3 mana, and we control the timing. At mana value 5, Gandalf can cast it for free once you control three legendary Wizards (X = 6). It was already my named first candidate for wipe #2. Swap: **Raise the Palisade in, Expressive Iteration out**. $0.

**4. More 2–3 card combos — yes.** I re-ran the full Spellbook check on the draft 99 (94 near-misses). Best completions:
- **Recommended: Fury Storm in, Loran's Escape out** (+$2.55 net). One card completes three 2-card combos with cards already in the list: with Storm-Kiln Artist (infinite Treasure and mana), with Archmage Emeritus (draw the deck), with Deekah (infinite tokens). The only prerequisite is having cast Gandalf once plus a second spell in hand. It is also a strong on-theme copy spell on its own.
- **Optional: Ghostly Flicker in, Time Stretch out** (−$2.63). Two-card infinite with Naru Meha: flash Naru in response to Flicker, and every re-entry copies the original still on the stack — infinite magecraft. I paired the cut with Time Stretch because it is the clunkiest buy (10 mana), but extra turns were your on-power pick, so this line is your call.
- **Considered and rejected**: Repercussion + Blasphemous Act — you own Repercussion, but the trigger is symmetric and this deck runs ~24 creatures, so a 13-damage wipe reflects roughly 13 × our own creature count back at us (it is also committed to eternal-agony). Searing Touch — needs Vadrik at power 4+ or Mizzix at four experience counters; too fragile. Kitsa + Dramatic Reversal and the Petals of Insight lines work but are weaker than Fury Storm; we can add them later.

**5. If you do not want it tuned down** — the draft is "low B4" because of four dials: no tutors, minimal fast mana, one compact combo, one-shot extra turns. To un-tune, in power-per-dollar order:
1. Take the combo lines above (~$7).
2. **Tutors — the biggest single jump**: Mystical Tutor $16.23 (Game Changer), Solve the Equation $3.77, Merchant Scroll $4.95. They find Sublime Epiphany or Fury Storm on demand, which turns the combos from incidental into reliable.
3. **Panoptic Mirror $26.39** — with Temporal Mastery, Alrund's Epiphany, and Time Stretch already in the list, it forms three different infinite-turn locks. I rejected it under the old tuning; at real B4 it belongs on the table.
4. Fast mana you pre-cleared: Mox Amber $79.81; second Ancient Tomb $134.91.
5. Free interaction: Fierce Guardianship $55.11 (Game Changer).

Game Changer note: the list has 0 GCs today and bracket 4 has no cap, so these additions change the label story, not compliance. My recommendation for "real B4 without silly money": combo lines + the three tutors + Panoptic Mirror, about $58 extra. If you pick any power items, I will come back with a named cut for each before writing anything.

## Review-gate results

- **Color identity / legality**: all 99 pre-validated against the 2026-08-15 mirror. No violations. 99 cards exactly.
- **Combos (Spellbook, full-list check)**: the list contains **one practical 2-card infinite: Naru Meha + Sublime Epiphany** (infinite copies → infinite draw with Archmage Emeritus → Vivi kills). It needs ~10 mana across two casts and we run no tutors for it, so assembly is slow — I judged it acceptable at 4-, but it is your call (checklist below). Kitsa + Insurrection is also technically infinite but depends on what creatures opponents have. Of the 94 near-miss combos, nearly all want a blink spell next to Naru Meha or a buyback spell next to Storm-Kiln/Mizzix; I **rejected the whole class deliberately** — completing them would push past the declared tuning. Panoptic Mirror lines (infinite-turn lock) are rejected hardest.
- **EDHREC closing diff** (~1,000 early decks already listed): high-synergy cards not in my first draft that I **added**: Flame of Anor, Wizard's Retort, Olórin's Searing Light, Wizard's Staff. **Deferred with reasons**: Call Forth the Tempest (perfect fit, but $36.17 day-one hype price — revisit when it settles), Path to Exile (6th spot removal, cheap add anytime), Azami, Lady of Scrolls (strong engine, UUU is the hardest cast we would run), Raise the Palisade ("bounce all non-Wizards" pseudo-wipe — first candidate if we want wipe #2), Akroma's Will (price ~$10), Gale / Alania / Talrand / Niv-Mizzet Parun / The Emperor of Palamecia (good wizards that lost slot fights on curve).
- **Your named cards**: Vivi in. Jeskai Revelation in. Firdoch Core **rejected** — it is a changeling but not legendary, so it never raises X; as a rock it loses to our 2-MV rocks. Non-legendary changelings all fail the same test. Legendary changelings (Orvar, Mistform Ultimus) do count but are weak bodies here — deferred; the 21-wizard density makes them unnecessary.
- **Hoser coverage**: the deck's hate classes are anti-spell stax pieces and commander locks, which arrive on artifacts and enchantments. Answers on both types: Generous Gift, Chaos Warp, Wear // Tear, Flame of Anor, Prismari Command. A Darksteel Mutation on Gandalf is destroyed by Generous Gift or Wear // Tear.
- **Commander-dependency**: with Gandalf locked, the deck still casts its big spells honestly through Baral, Stenn, Vadrik, Mizzix, Kaza (cost reduction), Vivi (ritual mana), and Johann (top-of-library casts).

**Data freshness (checked first, as asked)**
- The local Scryfall mirror was refreshed today after the DEC-486 fix: 31,830 oracle cards from the 2026-08-15 bulk file.
- It includes The Hobbit Eternal (`hoc`, released 2026-08-14 — Gandalf's set) and Lorwyn Eclipsed (`ecl`, 2026-01-23). No missing sets; all searching can run locally.

**Commander (oracle verified)**
Gandalf, Party Guest — {1}{U}{R}{W} 3/4 Legendary Avatar Wizard. At the beginning of combat on your turn, you may cast an instant or sorcery with mana value X or less from your hand for free, where X = 2 × the legendary Wizards you control. The trigger fires once per turn cycle (own turn only, DEC-477 basis). The free spell is *cast*, so cast-triggers (magecraft, Vivi, Adeliz, Veyran) all fire.

**Critical mass — the numbers**
- 136 legendary Wizard creatures exist in Jeskai identity; 64 at MV ≤ 3; 17 at MV 2. The pool is deep.
- Gandalf alone gives X=2. Each added legendary Wizard adds 2: Gandalf +2 others = X6; +3 = X8 (free Jeskai Revelation at MV 7).
- Draw odds (raw draws only, on the play, 10 cards seen by end of turn 4): 15 Wizard slots → 47% to hold 2+; 18 slots → 58%; 22 slots → 70%. Draw spells raise these. I recommend ~18 legendary-Wizard slots, most at MV ≤ 3.
- Payoff pool: 380 instants/sorceries at MV ≥ 6 in identity (65 at MV ≥ 8).

**Rulings on the named cards (all oracle-verified)**
- **Firdoch Core does NOT raise Gandalf's X.** It is a changeling (every creature type, so a Wizard) but it is not legendary, and Gandalf counts *legendary* Wizards only. The same applies to every non-legendary changeling. Remaining value: a 3-MV any-color mana rock. Verdict: manabase candidate only.
- The changeling route that does work: **legendary** changelings — Mistform Ultimus ({3}{U}) and Orvar, the All-Form ({3}{U}, changeling keyword verified; its copy trigger also loves our spell suite) both count. **Maskwood Nexus** ({4} artifact) makes all our creatures every type, so every legendary creature we run counts as a legendary Wizard. That is the real count-enabler.
- **Vivi Ornitier: definite include.** Legendary Wizard, adds X (= its power) in U/R once per turn, grows and pings each opponent on every noncreature spell. Also our best backup engine when Gandalf is locked.
- **Jeskai Revelation: strong include-candidate** as a free-cast payoff at Gandalf+3.

**Risks, and why they are manageable**
- Commander lock (Darksteel Mutation class, review step 9): the free-cast engine stops, but the deck still casts big spells through discount/ramp redundancy — Vadrik, Astral Archmage; Stenn, Paranoid Partisan; Baral; Vivi. I will name the covering cards in the build notes.
- Board wipes collapse X. Cheap legends rebuild fast; the 99 gets a protection suite.
- The engine is hand-fueled (the free cast comes from hand), so draw density is mandatory.
- EDHREC is near-empty for a commander released yesterday. The DEC-402 closing diff will still run, but on thin data; the census and first principles carry this build.
